analyses.name: Ralph Lauren Corporation
analyses.verdict: The highest-scoring setup in a 523-name universe, and the rare one where the base, the volume and the earnings all agree while the stock is still 4% below its high.

financials.period: Last full fiscal year (FY ended March 2026)
financials.summary: Ralph Lauren's last full fiscal year was a margin story more than a volume story. The multi-year repositioning — fewer promotional doors, more full-price direct-to-consumer selling, and disciplined inventory — continued to convert into gross-margin expansion, and average unit retail kept rising rather than being discounted back. Growth was led by international, with Asia and Europe outpacing North America, while the direct-to-consumer channel grew faster than wholesale and carried better economics. Operating leverage did the rest: the scan shows EPS growing +23.9% against revenue up +14.0%, which is the signature of a brand converting pricing power into profit rather than buying growth. Cash generation supported continued buybacks and a rising dividend, and the balance sheet ended the year with net cash comfortably covering lease and debt obligations. The reason the market is willing to pay 19x forward earnings for a apparel company is precisely this: the elevation strategy is showing up in the margin line year after year rather than as a one-off.

Revenue +14.0% YoY, led by international and direct-to-consumer
Forward P/E 19.0 — a reasonable multiple for mid-20s earnings growth
Gross margin expansion driven by full-price selling and higher average unit retail

accomplishments: Sustained brand elevation: fewer promotional channels, higher average unit retail, better gross margin
International expansion — Asia and Europe growing faster than the domestic base
Direct-to-consumer mix shift, capturing full retail economics instead of wholesale margin
Inventory discipline maintained through a promotional retail environment
Consistent capital return through buybacks and a growing dividend

journey_52w.summary: A year of steady, unglamorous accumulation ending in a textbook coil. RL traded as low as 280.32 and closed the latest session at 395.83 — a 41% advance off the low — and it did it in stages, not in a spike. Through the year the stock built six successive contractions, each shallower than the last, compressing to a final 2.1% range, which is the tightest quality base anywhere in this scan. The latest session resolved with volume at 2.07x average and a pocket-pivot flag, meaning institutions stepped in on the move rather than retail chasing it. It closes 4.2% below its 413.24 high with RSI at only 59.8 — a stock being accumulated, not chased. The one thing still missing is the relative-strength line, which remains 9% below its own high: leadership is being rebuilt here, not yet reclaimed.

analyses.name: PNC Financial Services Group
analyses.verdict: The most un-extended entry into the strongest sector in the market — 1% from a 52-week high with RSI at just 54.

financials.period: Last full fiscal year (FY ended December 2025)
financials.summary: PNC's last full fiscal year was defined by net interest income recovery and expense discipline. As deposit-repricing pressure from the prior tightening cycle eased and the securities portfolio rolled into higher-yielding paper, net interest margin expanded — the mechanism behind the +24.9% EPS growth the scan reports against +23.6% revenue growth. Fee income contributed a genuine second engine, with capital markets, treasury management and asset management all recovering as activity normalised. Credit performance was the quiet good news: consumer charge-offs normalised toward pre-pandemic levels rather than deteriorating, and commercial real estate reserves proved adequate against the sector's most-watched exposure. Capital generation was strong enough to support both dividend growth and buybacks while staying comfortably above regulatory CET1 minimums. Crucially, management is spending into the strength rather than harvesting it — the bank is midway through a roughly $2bn branch expansion programme and recently opened its 50th new branch, a signal of confidence in deposit-gathering economics that most regionals are not sending.

analyses.name: Science Applications International Corporation
analyses.verdict: A 52-week high at 11.3x forward earnings with EPS up 84% — and a revenue driver completely uncorrelated with everything else on today's list.

financials.period: Last full fiscal year (FY ended January/February 2026)
financials.summary: SAIC's last full fiscal year was a profitability story rather than a growth story, and the distinction matters. Revenue grew only +1.5% — government services is a slow-moving, recompete-driven market — but EPS grew +83.8%. That gap was closed by three things: a deliberate shift in the contract mix away from low-margin pass-through work toward higher-value systems integration, digital engineering and enterprise IT modernisation; disciplined bid-and-proposal spending that improved win rates on the contracts management actually wanted; and a consistent share-repurchase programme that concentrated the improved earnings across a smaller share count. Free cash flow conversion remained the hallmark of the model — this is an asset-light services business with limited capital intensity — and the balance sheet supported both buybacks and a modest dividend. Backlog remained the key forward indicator, underpinned by multi-year defence and civilian agency awards that give more revenue visibility than the single-digit growth rate suggests.

analyses.name: Howmet Aerospace Inc.
analyses.verdict: The strongest volume signature among the top-ten scorers, on the best structural story in industrials — but you are paying 47x for it.

financials.period: Last full fiscal year (FY ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Howmet's last full fiscal year captured the aerospace aftermarket cycle at close to its most favourable point. The company makes engineered components — jet engine airfoils, fastening systems, forged aluminium wheels — where qualification barriers are extreme and pricing is durable. Revenue grew +24.1% and EPS +33.0%, with the gap between them explained by mix and price: spare-parts demand from the engine aftermarket carries structurally higher margin than original-equipment production, and a global fleet flying more hours on older aircraft kept that mix favourable all year. Commercial aerospace led, defence contributed a steadier second leg, and the commercial transportation wheels business was the soft spot. Operating margin expanded meaningfully as volume leverage met a disciplined pricing posture on long-term agreements. Free cash flow supported deleveraging early in the year and then an increasing share of capital return through buybacks and a growing dividend. The structural point behind the valuation is simple: engine build rates and shop-visit schedules are visible years ahead, so Howmet's revenue is unusually forecastable for an industrial.

analyses.name: GE Aerospace
analyses.verdict: The highest-quality recurring revenue stream in industrials, at a full price — and the softest TradingView confirmation among my industrial picks.

financials.period: Last full fiscal year (FY ended December 2025)
financials.summary: GE Aerospace's first full fiscal years as a focused pure-play have validated the case for the breakup. The economics rest on a razor-and-blade model: engines are sold at thin or negative margin, and decades of high-margin spare parts and servicing follow. With the global fleet flying more hours and airlines extending the life of existing aircraft, shop visits and spare-parts demand ran strong all year, producing revenue growth of +21.1% and EPS growth of +19.4%. The commercial engines and services segment carried the result; defence and propulsion contributed a steadier, lower-margin second leg. Operating profit expanded as the services mix improved, and free cash flow conversion was strong enough to support a rising dividend alongside a substantial buyback. The installed base — tens of thousands of engines under long-term service agreements — is the real asset here, and it is why the market accords the company a multiple far above the industrial average.

analyses.name: Chevron Corporation
analyses.verdict: Buying the base rather than the breakout — RSI 52 and 9.6% below the high, with a live geopolitical bid underneath the whole sector.

financials.period: Last full fiscal year (FY ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Chevron's last full fiscal year was a recovery year across the integrated model, and the scan's headline figures reflect how depressed the comparison base was: EPS +322.9% on revenue +52.6%. Upstream carried the result, with production growth from the Permian and from major international projects arriving alongside a firmer realised price environment, while unit operating costs stayed disciplined. Downstream refining margins recovered from the prior year's trough as product cracks widened. The defining feature of the year was capital discipline: rather than chasing volume, management held capital expenditure within its stated framework, prioritised the highest-return barrels, and directed the resulting free cash flow to shareholders through a dividend increase and sustained buybacks. The balance sheet ended the year with low net gearing by historical standards, which is what allows the buyback to persist through commodity-price weakness — a genuine differentiator against smaller, more levered producers like Occidental.

financials.period: Last full fiscal year (FY ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Cheniere's last full fiscal year demonstrated why contracted LNG infrastructure earns a different multiple from commodity production. The bulk of liquefaction capacity is sold under long-term, take-or-pay sale-and-purchase agreements with fixed liquefaction fees, which means a large share of EBITDA is contracted years forward and largely insulated from spot gas volatility; the remaining uncontracted volumes provide upside when international spreads widen. The scan reports EPS +100.7% on revenue +22.9%, reflecting both higher volumes as trains ramped and the flow-through of a better spread environment on the merchant portion. Operationally the year was about execution on expansion — incremental liquefaction trains progressing toward completion, which is what converts today's capital spending into tomorrow's contracted cash flow. Financially the story was deleveraging plus capital return: management continued paying down project debt while sustaining buybacks and a growing dividend, a combination that only works because the underlying cash flows are contracted.

analyses.name: NVIDIA Corporation
analyses.verdict: Holding above both moving averages while its entire supply chain breaks down — the market is selling the equipment makers and paying for the compute deployers.

financials.period: Last full fiscal year (FY ended January 2026)
financials.summary: NVIDIA's last full fiscal year was, by any historical standard, an extraordinary one: the scan reports revenue +85.2% and EPS +214.5%. Data centre revenue dominated the mix, driven by accelerated-computing platform shipments to hyperscalers, cloud providers, sovereign programmes and enterprises building AI infrastructure. The economics of that mix are the key point — gross margins remained at levels almost unheard of for a hardware business, because the value sits in architecture and in the CUDA software ecosystem rather than in the silicon alone, and because customers buy full systems and networking rather than discrete chips. Networking, following the Mellanox integration, became a material revenue line in its own right. Gaming, professional visualisation and automotive continued as smaller, steadier contributors. Operating leverage was extreme: operating expenses grew far more slowly than revenue, so EPS grew at roughly two and a half times the revenue rate. Free cash flow generation funded large buybacks while the balance sheet retained a substantial net cash position. The forward multiple of 17.0x the scan reports is the striking number — that is a market-average multiple on a business that just grew earnings more than 200%, which tells you the market is discounting a sharp deceleration.
highlights: Revenue +85.2% YoY, led by data centre accelerated computing
EPS +214.5% YoY — roughly 2.5x the revenue growth rate, extreme operating leverage
Forward P/E 17.0 — a market multiple on hyper-growth, implying an expected deceleration
Gross margins sustained at levels atypical for hardware, protected by the CUDA software moat
Networking became a material second revenue engine post-Mellanox
Substantial free cash flow funding buybacks with a net cash balance sheet
Analyst consensus 1.30 — the most favourable rating in the entire scan

accomplishments: Established accelerated computing as the default architecture for AI training and inference
Maintained the CUDA ecosystem as a durable switching barrier against competing silicon
Scaled full-system and networking sales beyond discrete GPU shipments
Sustained hardware-atypical gross margins through a period of enormous volume growth
Executed large buybacks while retaining a net cash balance sheet

journey_52w.summary: The defining divergence in today's scan. NVDA traded as low as 164.98 and closed the latest session at 218.99 — 7.0% below its 235.47 high, holding above both its 50-DMA (205.82) and 200-DMA (193.59), with RSI at 63.1. Three-month momentum has cooled to +3.7%, so this has been a consolidation rather than an advance. What makes it remarkable is the contrast with its own supply chain: in the same universe, Applied Materials sits 27% below its high, Lam Research 29%, KLA 36%, Amkor 42%, Ichor 42%, MaxLinear 45% and ON Semiconductor 42% — and TradingView rates nearly all of them SELL. NVDA is rated BUY. Meanwhile the companies that buy compute are at or near highs: NetApp and Snowflake closed at 52-week highs, Dell is up 90% in three months, HPE 77%, Arista scores 90.0. The market has not repudiated AI; it has rotated from the picks-and-shovels layer to the deployment layer, and NVDA sits on the favoured side of that line.

analyses.name: Eli Lilly and Company
analyses.verdict: Revenue up 48% at a trillion-dollar market cap, and the stock is only 3.5% off its high with RSI at 52.

financials.period: Last full fiscal year (FY ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Lilly's last full fiscal year was dominated by the incretin franchise. Tirzepatide-based products across diabetes and obesity indications drove revenue growth of +47.7% — a rate essentially unheard of for a company of this scale — with EPS up +26.2%. The gap between the two growth rates is the important detail: it reflects deliberate reinvestment, principally an extraordinary manufacturing capital programme to expand fill-finish and active-ingredient capacity, plus continued heavy R&D spending on the pipeline behind the current franchise. In other words, margins were held back by choice rather than by pressure. Supply, not demand, remained the binding constraint for much of the year, and each incremental capacity addition converted more or less directly into revenue. Beyond incretins, the neuroscience and oncology portfolios provided secondary growth. The balance sheet supported both the capex programme and a rising dividend, though leverage increased relative to the company's historically conservative posture as the manufacturing build accelerated.
highlights: Revenue +47.7% YoY — exceptional for a company above $1tn in market value
EPS +26.2% YoY, deliberately held below revenue growth by reinvestment
Forward P/E 25.8 — a premium, but well below the historical peak multiple
Incretin franchise the dominant driver across diabetes and obesity indications
Manufacturing capacity expansion the largest use of capital; supply was the binding constraint
Neuroscience and oncology portfolios contributing secondary growth

accomplishments: Scaled the incretin franchise into one of the largest product families in pharmaceutical history
Executed an extraordinary manufacturing capacity expansion to relieve supply constraints
Advanced next-generation incretin candidates, including oral formulations, through the pipeline
Sustained dividend growth alongside a record capital-expenditure programme
Maintained pricing and formulary access in a politically hostile drug-pricing environment

journey_52w.summary: A near-doubling that has recently paused rather than broken. LLY traded as low as 621.26 and closed the latest session at 1191.94 — a 92% advance off the low — and sits just 3.5% below its 1235.56 high. Price is above both the 50-DMA (1155.49) and 200-DMA (1029.47), three-month momentum is +22.5%, and the latest session traded 1.27x average volume, so participation is real. What makes the current setup attractive is that RSI is only 52.1 after that advance: the stock has consolidated its gains sideways rather than giving them back, which is the healthier of the two ways to work off an overbought condition. The base is wide, though — a six-contraction VCP whose tightest contraction is still 8.6% — so a technically correct stop sits a long way below the entry. TradingView confirms at BUY (14 buy / 2 sell).

analyses.name: Dell Technologies Inc.
analyses.verdict: Up 90% in three months on the AI-server build-out — the clearest evidence that the market is paying for compute deployers, not equipment makers.

financials.period: Last full fiscal year (FY ended January/February 2026)
financials.summary: Dell's last full fiscal year was transformed by AI infrastructure demand. The scan reports revenue +87.5% and EPS +282.5%, figures that reflect the Infrastructure Solutions Group scaling AI-optimised server shipments to enterprises, cloud providers and sovereign programmes at a pace the traditional business had never produced. The honest caveat, and the one that defines the debate around the stock, is mix: AI server revenue carries materially lower gross margin than Dell's traditional storage and services business, because much of the bill of materials is accelerator silicon bought from suppliers and passed through. So revenue and shipment growth ran far ahead of gross-margin dollars, and the quality of that growth is genuinely lower than the headline suggests. Against that, the backlog and pipeline gave unusual forward visibility, the storage franchise provided a higher-margin counterweight, and the Client Solutions PC business stabilised as the commercial refresh cycle progressed. Cash generation supported continued dividend growth and buybacks. At 20.0x forward earnings, the market is applying a distinctly non-AI multiple to what has become, at the margin, an AI infrastructure business.
highlights: Revenue +87.5% and EPS +282.5% YoY on AI server demand
Forward P/E 20.0 — a conventional hardware multiple on AI-scale growth
AI-optimised server backlog provided unusual forward revenue visibility
Storage franchise supplied the higher-margin counterweight to pass-through server revenue
Client Solutions stabilised on the commercial PC refresh cycle
Cash generation supported both dividend growth and buybacks

accomplishments: Scaled AI-optimised server shipments to enterprise, cloud and sovereign customers
Built a substantial AI infrastructure backlog providing forward revenue visibility
Stabilised the Client Solutions PC business through the commercial refresh cycle
Maintained storage share as the profit engine alongside lower-margin server growth
Sustained dividend growth and buybacks through a period of heavy working-capital demand

journey_52w.summary: One of the largest advances in the entire scan. DELL traded as low as 110.54 and closed the latest session at 437.65 — nearly a quadruple — with three-month momentum of +90.4%. The 200-DMA sits at 219.54 against a 412.50 50-DMA, a gap that illustrates how violent and how recent the re-rating has been. The stock closed 6.3% below its 467.27 high with RSI at a surprisingly moderate 57.6, meaning it has consolidated the move rather than continuing to spike. There is no clear VCP — this is a momentum trend, not a tight-base breakout, and it should be sized accordingly. Its importance in today's scan is as evidence: alongside NetApp at a 52-week high, Snowflake at a 52-week high and HPE up 77% in three months, DELL is the proof that capital rotating out of semiconductor equipment (AMAT -27%, LRCX -29%, KLAC -36%) went into the companies that deploy compute rather than out of AI altogether.

analyses.name: Liquidia Corporation
analyses.verdict: The third-highest score in a 523-name universe and by far the highest-risk name on the list — it reports in five days with 17% of its float sold short.

financials.period: Last full fiscal year (FY ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Liquidia's last full fiscal year was its transition from a development-stage company to a commercial one, which is why the scan's revenue growth figure of +4158% is arithmetically true but analytically meaningless — it is growth from a near-zero base as the company's dry-powder inhaled treprostinil product for pulmonary arterial hypertension and pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease moved into commercial launch. The financial story of such a year is not profitability, which remains absent, but three things: the pace of prescriber adoption and patient starts; the gross-to-net dynamics as payer coverage was negotiated; and the cash runway, since commercial-stage biotechs burn heavily on salesforce build-out and launch marketing. The company spent the year building specialty distribution relationships and pulmonology prescriber coverage, while continuing to defend and pursue intellectual property positions against the incumbent — litigation being an unavoidable feature of this therapeutic area. A forward P/E of 15.4 implies the market is already underwriting a substantial and rapid ramp toward profitability, which is precisely what makes the upcoming report consequential.
highlights: Revenue growth of +4158% — real, but off a near-zero pre-commercial base
Transition from development-stage to commercial-stage during the year
Forward P/E 15.4 — implies the market already assumes a steep, successful ramp
Salesforce and specialty distribution built out for the pulmonology channel
Payer coverage and gross-to-net negotiation the key determinant of realised revenue
Analyst consensus 1.38 — notably favourable for a single-product company

accomplishments: Completed the transition from development-stage to commercial-stage operations
Launched its inhaled treprostinil product into the pulmonary hypertension market
Built specialty pharmacy distribution and pulmonology prescriber coverage from scratch
Advanced its intellectual property position in a heavily litigated therapeutic area
Achieved a market valuation of roughly $8bn on the strength of the launch trajectory

journey_52w.summary: One of the most violent advances in the scan. LQDA traded as low as 19.21 and closed the latest session at 89.42 — a 365% advance, closing exactly at its 52-week high. Three-month momentum is +111.5%, and the 200-DMA sits at 46.23, meaning the stock trades at nearly double its own long-term average with no meaningful technical support anywhere close. The relative-strength line is up 12.7% over four weeks and the base is a four-contraction VCP tightened to 5.2%, so the pattern is genuinely constructive. But the risk profile is the story: 17.2% of the float is sold short with a HIGH squeeze reading, which explains part of the velocity, and earnings land in five days. TradingView rates it BUY (14 buy / 4 sell) — supportive, but with more dissent than it shows on the large-cap leaders. This earns its place on the list on merit and does not earn a full-size position.
